title: Surgical scope paring for Console observability surfaces (dashboards, tracing, cost snapshot)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
We need to ship a minimal, useful observability surface for the Redwood Console while keeping delivery time and engineering cost low. Previous scope included full route-level token breakdown, interactive cost explorer, granular trace timelines, and retention-backed dashboards. That scope is too large for the current cycle and risks delaying foundational rollout for Dedicated and Private customers.

Proposal (surgical cuts):
1) Dashboards: deliver a fixed set of 4 summary cards (Traffic Overview, Latency P95, Error Rate, Cost Snapshot by route) instead of a full card editor and arbitrary card templates. Cards are read-only for alpha and link to the raw data view (on-demand CSV / raw query) for power users.
2) Tracing: ship a 1% probabilistic sampling with a deterministic trace link for any sampled request. Full trace search and deep flamegraphs deferred. Provide a lightweight trace viewer with span list, timestamps, and the payload link.
3) Cost breakdown: show a top-level cost snapshot per route for the last 24h and 7d with delta indicators and a small "explain cost" modal that surfaces the main drivers (batching, model variant, tokens). Defer token-level per-request breakdown and perc-route historical trends to v2.
4) Rollouts & fallbacks: include rollout flags in the console to enable/disable the snapshot/trace surfaces per org for easier rollback.

Rationale:
- Maximizes signal-to-effort: teams get actionable guardrails without full analytics platform work.
- Preserves essential safety: sampling + deterministic links allow debugging while keeping storage and cost low.
- Allows iterative expansion: we can add interactive cards, deeper trace exploration, and token-level costs after the alpha.

Non-goals (explicitly out of scope for this ticket):
- Card editor or custom card definitions
- Full trace search across all requests
- Long-term cost retention dashboards
acceptance_criteria: A1: Four console cards (Traffic Overview, Latency P95, Error Rate, Cost Snapshot) render for org admins with real-time values from the last 24h.
A2: Cost Snapshot shows per-route top-level cost and a modal explaining top 3 cost drivers; modal content derived from existing billing enrichment pipeline (no new ETL).
A3: Tracing surface accepts sampled traces (1% sampling default). Sampled traces include a deterministic link to raw request payload stored in S3/GCS for on-demand download.
A4: Rollout flags exist in admin settings to opt an org in/out of the new surfaces and will flip within 10 minutes of change.
A5: Console feature ships with documentation page (confluence) and an inline "Why am I seeing this?" help tooltip explaining sampling and data freshness.
A6: Performance: new dashboard cards load under 1.2s for 95th percentile in us-west region on staging data with existing query caches enabled.
A7: Security: access to trace payloads respects existing RBAC and KMS-encrypted payloads remain encrypted; no new secrets are introduced.
A8: We have an instrumented telemetry event for "console.observability.surface_loaded" and sampling metrics to verify 1% sampling is respected.
A9: Product sign-off from Observability PM and Eng lead recorded in comments and linked PR merged into console-alpha branch.
updates: 2025-01-23 - Aisha Patel: Initial draft and prioritization rationale posted. Pitched surgical cuts to leadership during PM sync.

2025-01-27 - Liam Oconnor: Eng estimates reviewed with infra and frontend. Backend QA raised concerns about storage growth for sampled payloads; agreed to use short-lived signed URLs and store only minimal indices.
2025-01-29 - Design review (Maya Chen): Delivered card mocks for read-only snapshots; suggested adding a small inline help icon to the Cost Snapshot card to reduce support questions.

2025-02-01 - Security review (Ravi Singh): Confirmed RBAC behavior; recommended KMS integration for payload links and audit logging — security review not blocking for alpha if KMS is enabled by default for orgs with compliance tier.

2025-02-03 - Liam Oconnor: Implementation plan approved. Backend work split into (a) snapshot aggregation job + API, (b) trace sampler + signed URL generator. Frontend work scoped to read-only card components and simplified trace viewer.
2025-02-05 - Aisha Patel: Scope locked for alpha. Open follow-ups created for v2 features (card editor, trace search, token-level cost) in PM backlog.
